summary: The ADR's decision, its measurements and its tree citations verified true against the code (SegmentKey.timestampMillis == Accumulator.firstAppendMillis via createdAt = view.getLong(16); SegmentPublisher.sequence an instance AtomicLong; SegmentCommit is (String,List<RunCommit>) with only a non-empty check; the golden holds bins/a.seg and bins/b.seg; BatchingSequencerTest:259-261 is from(pod0,0)/from(pod1,0) with hasSize(2); BatchedCommitDeltaTest:152 is new CommitRequest("pod"+pod, 0, ...); Checkpoint.decode is version != VERSION; CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest:117 is bytes[7]=1; CheckpointTest:169 asserts < 64 KiB at 1,600 streams; CheckpointWriter:129 is pods.merge(request.podId(), request.flushSeq(), Math::max); DefaultIngest:349 evaluates flushSeq++ as the commit argument and the catch discards `published`; ChainReplay:50 is the "never GET at all" javadoc; ChainEntry:50 records the ADR-0032 reservation consumed; ADR-0028:130 leaves the version path open; ADR-0031 bounds the collision to waste, not idempotency). Two majors remain: an exhaustiveness claim about the sweep that is false, and a new pod-axis GET whose only bound is a sentence addressed to a future session.

findings.finding: The M4.10c hand-off paragraph declares itself exhaustive -- "THE LIST IS THE AUTHORITY, NOT A COUNT" and "`git grep -n 'podId, flushSeq' -- '*.java'` finds every one EXCEPT the sentence promising the record shape does not change, which spans `Sequencer.java:48-50`". Measured: the grep misses TWO sites, not one. `CommitRequest.java:35-36` reads "@param flushSeq that node's own monotonic flush counter. Together with {@code podId} it identifies this commit uniquely across the fleet" -- it matches no line of that grep, it is absent from the list, and it is the strongest statement in the tree of the exact premise ADR-0036 measures false. `git grep -n 'uniquely across the fleet' -- '*.java'` returns it and nothing else.
findings.failure_scenario: An M4.10c session works the list, adds `incarnationId` to `CommitRequest`, and lands. The record's own class javadoc then carries `@param incarnationId` three lines below a sentence asserting that `(podId, flushSeq)` alone identifies a commit uniquely across the fleet -- the property the new field exists to supply. The same notes warn twelve lines later that "AN M4.10d SESSION READS THE SEAM, NOT THIS FILE"; that session reads CommitRequest, is told the pair is fleet-unique, keys dedup on the pair, and every M4 fixture is single-incarnation so the suite stays green while a restarted pod's flushSeq 0 is SUPPRESSED -- the primary harm this ADR exists to prevent. Mitigating fact, stated rather than hidden: :19 and :36 sit inside the SAME javadoc block, so a careful editor may see it anyway; the defect is that the paragraph certifies it does not exist. Fix is one entry plus correcting "EXCEPT" to name both.

findings.finding: The decision adds a commit-path GET on an axis the task's own property list forbids ("It must add no COMMIT-PATH request that scales with the number of pods -- the rate M4.7 was built to remove"), and the only thing bounding it is prose addressed to a future session: "M4.10d must issue AT MOST ONE GET per distinct `(epoch, sequence)` per batch; N GETs of one object inside one `commitAll` is cost.md R5 and R4 on the commit path, on the pod axis M4.7 exists to remove." Nothing checkable is added for it. Measured against the SPEC this same commit edits: acceptance criterion 9 (SPEC.md:443) counts "the number of commit-chain **PUTs**" only, and the sole pod-axis test row (SPEC.md:480) is "PUT count unchanged from 1 pod to 6". Criterion 6 was rewritten in this diff (SPEC.md:418-427) and the T0 row at :478 was rewritten, and neither gained a request-count clause. The GET axis introduced here is therefore covered by no criterion and no T-row.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10d implements the obvious loop -- `for (CommitRequest r : batch) if (isReplay(r)) delta = read(store, keyFor(pointer(r)));`. Under M4.7 a batched delta is one object shared by the whole window, so after one ambiguous PUT all N pods in the window retry, all N slots name the same `(epoch, sequence)`, and one `commitAll` issues N GETs of ONE object. Criterion 9 stays green (PUT count unchanged), the T1 batching row stays green (PUTs), criterion 6 and the T0 idempotency row stay green (offsets are correct), and the pod-axis request rate M4.7 was built to remove is back as GETs -- cost.md R4 and R5, on the commit path, invisible to every gate. The ADR names this exact mutation and then leaves it to be remembered. The fix in this commit is one clause on criterion 6 or one T-row ("replay handling issues at most one GET per distinct pointed delta per batch, asserted through CountingBinStore | N GETs of one shared delta"), in the file the diff already opens; the alternative is a staged baselines/review.txt entry arguing the axis.

findings.finding: "AND THE THREE DESCRIPTIVE `SPEC.md` SITES ARE THIS ROW'S: `:55`, `:501` and `:511`". Measured against the staged SPEC.md: the three sites are 55, 503 and 513. :501 is the "I5 asserted vacuously" risk row and :511 is a markdown table separator `|---|---|`. The drift is exactly 2 and was introduced by THIS round's own fix: the criterion-6 rewrite grew that hunk by two more lines than the version the citation was written against, shifting everything below it.
findings.failure_scenario: An M4.10c session opens SPEC.md:511, finds a table separator, opens :501, finds a paragraph about I5 that never mentions `(podId, flushSeq)`, concludes the citation is stale and drops the item. SPEC.md:513 ("M4.1 | ... the commit request carries `(podId, flushSeq, …)`") and :503 then keep describing the seam in the pre-M4.10c shape after M4.10c lands. Same class as the finding this paragraph opens with ("an earlier sweep missed by stopping at markdown"): a pointer that resolves to the wrong line.

findings.finding: "Within that reading, so one number gives an **unbounded-depth** window: a replay of any earlier commit is caught" -- the sentence does not parse; the stray "so" is a leftover from inserting the REFUSAL-IS-NOT-PROOF clause immediately before it. It is inside the Decision section, which is the normative text of an accepted ADR.
findings.failure_scenario: The sentence that states the detection depth -- the property the whole one-number design rests on, and the one an M4.10d session must implement exactly -- is the one sentence in the Decision that a reader has to reconstruct. A reader who reconstructs it as "within that reading, one number gives" gets the intent; a reader who attaches it to the preceding refusal clause reads it as a qualifier on refusals and bounds detection to the last applied flush, which is the opposite of what the ADR decides.

findings.finding: Answering a replay now depends on GETting a chain entry that may sit arbitrarily far below the newest checkpoint, and nothing states that the pointed delta must OUTLIVE the checkpoint that names it. The ADR is careful about the other lifetime question in this area (a window recovered from a pre-change checkpoint, :189-199) and silent on this one, while SPEC.md:421-423 upgrades it to an unconditional promise: "THE POINTER IS RECORDED FOR EVERY APPLIED COMMIT, so a replay of a pod's most recent applied `flushSeq` is ALWAYS answered".
findings.failure_scenario: `Checkpoint.oldestRetainedOffset` is carried today for M7 (`Checkpoint.java:30-33`: "nothing consumes it before M7"), and cost.md R8 makes retention a dial in hours. When M7 trims chain entries the checkpoint has already absorbed -- precisely the entries ChainReplay:50 says are "never GET at all", so nothing else would notice their absence -- a slot pointing into a trimmed delta produces a missing-object IOException on the answering path, which `CheckpointCursor`-style handling reports as "the store is unreachable". SPEC criterion 6's ALWAYS becomes false, and M7 has no way to learn the constraint because no artifact records it. One sentence in Consequences ("a delta named by a live checkpoint slot must not be trimmed") closes it.
